345	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
346	# History integrity checks
347	#
348	# Every ``require_intact_history_*`` check scans the same record list of
349	# the same target batch entry, so the shared mechanics live in two
350	# helpers: ``_iter_history_records`` reads the list once, rejects a
351	# missing list or a non-object row and yields ``(position, record)``
352	# pairs; ``_corruption_prefix`` and ``_record_ref`` assemble the common
353	# "Batch history is corrupted: batch ..." message parts.  The checks
354	# themselves stay separate passes and keep their original order on the
355	# undo path — duplicate digests, then revisions, then labels, then
356	# changed flags — each reporting its first problem in record order.
357	# Re-submission (``resolve_re_submission``) reuses the two checks that
358	# verdict needs, in the same order: duplicate digests, then labels, both
359	# running before the same-content replay / different-content conflict
360	# decision.
361	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
362	
363	
364	def _corruption_prefix(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:
365	    """Shared prefix of every batch-history corruption message."""
366	    return f"Batch history is corrupted: batch {entry.get('batch')!r}"
367	
368	
369	def _record_ref(record: Mapping[str, Any], position: int | None = None) -> str:
370	    """Locate a history record by sample digest and optional 1-based position."""
371	    ref = f"sample {record.get('sha256')}"
372	    if position is not None:
373	        ref += f", record #{position}"
374	    return ref
375	
376	
377	def _iter_history_records(
378	    entry: Mapping[str, Any],
379	) -> Iterator[tuple[int, Mapping[str, Any]]]:
380	    """Yield ``(position, record)`` for each row of a batch history entry.
381	
382	    This is the shared front half of every integrity check: the entry
383	    must carry a record list and every row must be an object.  Positions
384	    are 1-based, matching the record numbers used in error messages.
385	    """
386	    prefix = _corruption_prefix(entry)
387	    records = entry.get("records")
388	    if not isinstance(records, list):
389	        # validate_history() already rules this out; defend direct callers.
390	        raise BatchError(f"{prefix}: missing records")
391	    for position, record in enumerate(records, start=1):
392	        if not isinstance(record, dict):
393	            raise BatchError(f"{prefix}: malformed record")
394	        yield position, record
395	
396	
397	def require_intact_history_records(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
398	    """Reject a batch entry whose records are not one row per sample.
399	
400	    Undo pins every stored record to a sample content digest, so a digest
401	    may occur at most once in the target batch: a duplicated row — even a
402	    byte-for-byte copy, or a copy of a record that never changed a label —
403	    would otherwise restore the same sample more than once, bump its label
404	    revision repeatedly and inflate the restored count.  Duplicates are
405	    therefore batch-history corruption, never records to merge or
406	    de-duplicate.  The decision is independent of the labels, the
407	    before/after labels and the record's ``changed`` flag: the content
408	    digest alone decides.
409	
410	    The whole record list is scanned, so rows preceding the repeat are
411	    checked too and a restorable row at the front can never mask a later
412	    duplicate.  On a repeat the error names the batch number, the sample's
413	    full digest and both 1-based record positions; nothing is repaired.
414	
415	    Callers must run this before any success-shaped short-circuit (such as
416	    an already-undone batch or a same-number replay), so corruption can
417	    never be masked by a repeated-undo success or by a replay whose
418	    set-based content comparison would collapse the duplicate into one.
419	    """
420	    seen: dict[str, int] = {}
421	    for position, record in _iter_history_records(entry):
422	        digest = record.get("sha256")
423	        if digest in seen:
424	            raise BatchError(
425	                f"{_corruption_prefix(entry)}, sample {digest} "
426	                f"appears more than once, at record #{seen[digest]} and "
427	                f"record #{position}"
428	            )
429	        seen[digest] = position
430	
431	
432	def require_intact_history_revisions(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
433	    """Reject a batch entry whose records lack a sound pinned ``rev``.
434	
435	    Every record — changed or not — must carry ``rev`` as a genuine
436	    non-negative integer, since undo pins each changed sample to the
437	    revision it had at the end of the batch.  This is integrity damage,
438	    unlike the *manifest's* optional revision (see
439	    :func:`item_revision`, which keeps the legacy missing-means-zero
440	    behaviour): a bad row is reported with the batch number, the sample's
441	    full digest and the exact ``rev`` problem, and nothing is repaired.
442	
443	    Callers must run this before any success-shaped short-circuit (such as
444	    an already-undone batch), so corruption can never be masked by a
445	    repeated-undo success.
446	    """
447	    for _position, record in _iter_history_records(entry):
448	        problem = describe_history_revision_problem(
449	            record.get("rev"), present="rev" in record
450	        )
451	        if problem is not None:
452	            raise BatchError(
453	                f"{_corruption_prefix(entry)}, "
454	                f"{_record_ref(record)}: {problem}"
455	            )
456	
457	
458	def describe_missing_history_labels(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str | None:
459	    """Describe which of a history record's before/after labels are absent.
460	
461	    Every batch-history sample record must spell out both ``old`` (the
462	    label before the batch) and ``new`` (the label after it).  Only key
463	    presence is judged here: an explicitly saved ``null`` or empty string
464	    is a recorded unlabeled label, never a missing field.  Returns
465	    ``None`` when both keys are present.
466	    """
467	    missing = [key for key in ("old", "new") if key not in record]
468	    if not missing:
469	        return None
470	    if len(missing) == 2:
471	        return "missing 'old' and 'new' labels"
472	    return f"missing {missing[0]!r} label"
473	
474	
475	def require_intact_history_labels(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
476	    """Reject a batch entry whose records lack a saved before/after label.
477	
478	    Undo restores and counts samples purely from what the target batch's
479	    history rows say: a changed row is restored from ``new`` back to
480	    ``old``, an unchanged row is left alone.  That is only meaningful
481	    when every row explicitly carries both labels, so a row missing
482	    ``old``, ``new`` or both is batch-history corruption — never an
483	    unlabeled-to-unlabeled no-op to skip, and never something to guess
484	    from the sample's current label.  The error names the batch number,
485	    the sample's full SHA-256 digest, the record's 1-based position
486	    inside the target batch and which of ``old``/``new`` (or both) is
487	    absent; nothing is repaired, rewritten or restored.
488	
489	    An explicitly saved ``null`` or empty string stays legal: both mean
490	    unlabeled, as does a literal class named ``unlabeled`` stay an
491	    ordinary label.  Only a missing key is damage.
492	
493	    The whole record list is scanned in order — unchanged rows and rows
494	    behind restorable ones included — so a complete row at the front can
495	    never mask a damaged one further back, and no sample is restored
496	    before the damage is found.
497	
498	    Callers must run this before any success-shaped short-circuit (such
499	    as an already-undone batch or a same-number replay), so corruption
500	    can never be masked by a success verdict or swallowed by a conflict.
501	    """
502	    for position, record in _iter_history_records(entry):
503	        problem = describe_missing_history_labels(record)
504	        if problem is not None:
505	            raise BatchError(
506	                f"{_corruption_prefix(entry)}, "
507	                f"{_record_ref(record, position)}: {problem}"
508	            )
509	
510	
511	def history_labels_equal(old: Any, new: Any) -> bool:
512	    """Whether two stored history labels describe the same category.
513	
514	    The decision uses the labels saved in the history record itself, never
515	    a sample's current label: ``null`` and the empty string both mean
516	    unlabeled and are therefore equal, while every other value is compared
517	    as the exact original string — case, surrounding whitespace, Chinese
518	    text and path separators all keep their meaning, and a real class
519	    literally named ``unlabeled`` never equals unlabeled.
520	    """
521	    return normalize_label(old) == normalize_label(new)
522	
523	
524	def describe_history_change_problem(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str | None:
525	    """Describe why a history record's ``changed`` flag contradicts old/new.
526	
527	    The flag must agree with the before/after labels saved on that same
528	    record: differing labels require ``changed: true`` and equal labels
529	    require ``changed: false``.  Returns ``None`` when the flag is
530	    consistent.  The stored labels are validated upstream as strings or
531	    ``None`` and the flag as a boolean, so no type guessing happens here.
532	    """
533	    actually_changed = not history_labels_equal(record["old"], record["new"])
534	    old_label = normalize_label(record["old"])
535	    new_label = normalize_label(record["new"])
536	    if actually_changed and not record["changed"]:
537	        return (
538	            f"'changed' is false but the before/after labels differ: "
539	            f"{render_label(old_label)!r} -> {render_label(new_label)!r}"
540	        )
541	    if not actually_changed and record["changed"]:
542	        return (
543	            f"'changed' is true but the before/after labels are identical: "
544	            f"{render_label(old_label)!r}"
545	        )
546	    return None
547	
548	
549	def require_intact_history_changes(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
550	    """Reject a batch entry whose ``changed`` flags belie old/new labels.
551	
552	    Undo restores a sample based on what the history row says the batch
553	    did: a row marked changed is restored from ``new`` back to ``old`` and
554	    counted, while a row marked unchanged is never restored.  So the flag
555	    must match the before/after labels saved on that row — judging from the
556	    record's own stored labels rather than any sample's current label:
557	
558	    * differing old/new (``null`` and ``""`` being the same unlabeled
559	      spelling) require ``changed: true``;
560	    * identical old/new require ``changed: false``.
561	
562	    A row that claims a change with identical labels would make undo count
563	    and restore a sample the batch never touched; a row that hides a real
564	    change would leave the sample at its post-batch label while the batch
565	    is recorded undone.  Both are batch-history corruption: the error names
566	    the batch number, the sample's full SHA-256 digest and the record's
567	    1-based position inside the target batch, together with the exact
568	    contradiction, and nothing is repaired.
569	
570	    The whole record list is scanned in order, so a restorable row at the
571	    front can never mask a contradiction further back.
572	
573	    Callers must run this before any success-shaped short-circuit (such as
574	    an already-undone batch), so corruption can never be masked by a
575	    repeated-undo success.
576	    """
577	    for position, record in _iter_history_records(entry):
578	        problem = describe_history_change_problem(record)
579	        if problem is not None:
580	            raise BatchError(
581	                f"{_corruption_prefix(entry)}, "
582	                f"{_record_ref(record, position)}: {problem}"
583	            )
584	
585	
586	def find_unique_history_entry(
587	    number: str, batches: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]
588	) -> Mapping[str, Any] | None:
589	    """Find the single history entry whose number is ``number``.
590	
591	    An undo target must name exactly one batch.  Matching is on the batch
592	    number's saved raw string — no trimming of surrounding whitespace and
593	    no case folding — so the whole list is scanned with exact equality
594	    rather than stopping at the first hit: a second entry carrying the
595	    same number, whether adjacent to the first or separated by other
596	    batches, makes the target ambiguous.  Such a history is corrupted no
597	    matter what the two entries contain — identical record content,
598	    different samples, different label changes or differing undo states
599	    are all refusal, never a reason to pick the first, the last or the
600	    still-active one, and never something to merge.
601	
602	    Returns the unique entry, or ``None`` when the number does not occur.
603	    On a repeat the error names the user-given batch number and the two
604	    1-based positions of the conflicting entries in the full history
605	    list, so neither record is undone, preferred or repaired.  Callers
606	    must run this before every per-entry integrity check and before the
607	    already-undone short-circuit: even an entry already marked undone
608	    leaves the number ambiguous and must surface this instead.
609	    """
610	    positions = [
611	        position
612	        for position, entry in enumerate(batches, start=1)
613	        if isinstance(entry, Mapping) and entry.get("batch") == number
614	    ]
615	    if not positions:
616	        return None
617	    if len(positions) >= 2:
618	        raise BatchError(
619	            "Batch history is corrupted: batch number "
620	            f"{number!r} appears more than once, at batch #{positions[0]} "
621	            f"and batch #{positions[1]}"
622	        )
623	    return batches[positions[0] - 1]
624	
625	
626	def empty_history() -> dict[str, Any]:
627	    return {"schema_version": BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION, "batches": []}
628	
629	
630	def validate_history(data: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
631	    """Validate a loaded batch history payload; return it unchanged."""
632	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("schema_version") != BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION:
633	        raise BatchError("Unsupported batch history")
634	    batches = data.get("batches")
635	    if not isinstance(batches, list):
636	        raise BatchError("Malformed batch history")
637	    for entry in batches:
638	        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
639	            raise BatchError("Malformed batch history entry")
640	        if not isinstance(entry.get("batch"), str) or not entry["batch"].strip():
641	            raise BatchError("Malformed batch history entry: missing batch number")
642	        if not isinstance(entry.get("records"), list):
643	            raise BatchError("Malformed batch history entry: missing records")
644	        changed_count = entry.get("changed_count")
645	        if not isinstance(changed_count, int) or isinstance(changed_count, bool):
646	            raise BatchError("Malformed batch history entry: bad changed_count")
647	        if not isinstance(entry.get("undone"), bool):
648	            raise BatchError("Malformed batch history entry: bad undone flag")
649	        for record in entry["records"]:
650	            if not isinstance(record, dict):
651	                raise BatchError("Malformed batch history record")
652	            if not isinstance(record.get("sha256"), str):
653	                raise BatchError("Malformed batch history record: bad digest")
654	            for key in ("old", "new"):
655	                value = record.get(key)
656	                if value is not None and not isinstance(value, str):
657	                    raise BatchError("Malformed batch history record: bad label")
658	            if not isinstance(record.get("changed"), bool):
659	                raise BatchError("Malformed batch history record: bad changed flag")
660	    return data

"""Batch label-update submission, validation and history.

A batch file is a UTF-8 JSON object of the form::

    {
      "batch": "non-empty batch number",
      "changes": [
        {"sha256": "<full SHA-256 digest>", "old": <string or null>,
         "new": <string or null>}
      ]
    }

``null`` and the empty string both mean "unlabeled"; any other string is
taken literally (including Chinese text and a class named ``unlabeled``).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Callable, Iterator, Mapping, Sequence

BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BatchResolution:
    """One record's verdict, produced before anything is written.

    ``current`` is the label read once during verification and ``changed``
    is whether ``new`` differs from it.  A resolution never references the
    manifest item or its revision, so the decision stays independent of
    the later workspace save.
    """

    sha256: str
    old: str | None
    new: str | None
    current: str | None
    changed: bool


class BatchError(ValueError):
    """A batch submission or undo request is invalid."""


def normalize_label(label: Any) -> str | None:
    """Map the two unlabeled spellings to ``None``; keep strings literal.

    Raises :class:`BatchError` for anything that is not a string or ``None``.
    """
    if label is None or label == "":
        return None
    if isinstance(label, str):
        return label
    raise BatchError(f"label must be a string or null, got {label!r}")


def render_label(label: str | None) -> str:
    """Human-readable rendering for messages."""
    return "unlabeled" if label is None else label


def parse_batch_file(data: Any) -> tuple[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    """Validate a parsed batch payload; return ``(number, records)``.

    Each record is ``{"sha256": str, "old": str | None, "new": str | None}``
    with labels normalized (``None`` for unlabeled).  Structural problems,
    an empty batch number and duplicate digests are all rejected here.
    """
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise BatchError("batch file must contain a JSON object")
    number = data.get("batch")
    if not isinstance(number, str) or not number.strip():
        raise BatchError("batch number must be a non-empty string")
    changes = data.get("changes")
    if not isinstance(changes, list):
        raise BatchError("batch file must contain a 'changes' list")

    records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for index, change in enumerate(changes):
        location = f"change #{index + 1}"
        if not isinstance(change, dict):
            raise BatchError(
                f"{location}: must be an object with 'sha256', 'old' and 'new'"
            )
        if not all(key in change for key in ("sha256", "old", "new")):
            raise BatchError(
                f"{location}: must contain 'sha256', 'old' and 'new' keys"
            )
        digest = change["sha256"]
        if not isinstance(digest, str) or not digest:
            raise BatchError(f"{location}: 'sha256' must be a non-empty string")
        if digest in seen:
            raise BatchError(f"{location}: duplicate sample {digest}")
        seen.add(digest)
        old = normalize_label(change["old"])
        new = normalize_label(change["new"])
        records.append({"sha256": digest, "old": old, "new": new})
    return number, records


def content_key(records: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> frozenset[tuple[str, str | None, str | None]]:
    """Order- and spelling-insensitive identity of a batch's content.

    Two submissions with the same number are considered the same batch
    when their record sets compare equal here: list order does not matter
    and ``null`` vs ``""`` does not matter.  Labels are normalized on both
    sides before comparing, so the equality also holds across the two
    places records come from — freshly parsed records (already normalized
    to ``None``) and history rows loaded from disk, which may have legally
    saved either unlabeled spelling.  Every other string is kept exactly,
    so a real class named ``unlabeled`` never matches an unlabeled record
    and case, surrounding whitespace, Chinese text and path separators
    stay significant.
    """
    return frozenset(
        (
            record["sha256"],
            normalize_label(record["old"]),
            normalize_label(record["new"]),
        )
        for record in records
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Submission rules
#
# Each stage is a pure function of parsed records and the state passed to
# it; none of them mutate the manifest or the history.  The stages line up
# with the conditions that reject a submission, in their original order:
#
#   1. reject_unknown_samples  — records naming no registered sample
#   2. resolve_re_submission   — same-number history: the existing entry
#                                must list each sample once (corruption
#                                refusal) and save both labels on every
#                                record (corruption refusal), then replay
#                                or conflict
#   3. verify_records          — one current-label pass: old-label
#                                mismatches reject the whole batch; the
#                                surviving resolutions also decide which
#                                records actually change
#   4. apply_resolutions       — the only mutating stage (store layer)
#   5. build_history_entry / result_payload — result/history assembly
#
# "Current label" is read exactly once for the whole submission (stage 3),
# so verification and the change decision never process it twice.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# A current-label lookup: full digest -> normalized current label (or
# ``None`` when the digest names no registered sample).
CurrentLabels = Callable[[str], str | None]


def reject_unknown_samples(
    records: list[dict[str, Any]], known: Callable[[str], bool]
) -> None:
    """Reject the batch if any record names a sample that is not registered.

    The first unknown record is reported, in submission order.
    """
    for record in records:
        if not known(record["sha256"]):
            raise BatchError(f"sample not found: {record['sha256']}")


def resolve_re_submission(
    number: str,
    records: list[dict[str, Any]],
    existing: dict[str, Any] | None,
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Handle a batch number already present in history.

    Equal content (per :func:`content_key`) replays the first submission's
    result without touching the manifest — even when samples have since
    changed — while different content conflicts.  Returns the replay
    result, or ``None`` when the number is free.

    Integrity is refused before either verdict.  The same-number entry
    must list every sample at most once (see
    :func:`require_intact_history_records`): a content digest appearing on
    a second record is batch-history corruption, and it has to be caught
    here because :func:`content_key` compares record *sets*, so a
    duplicated row would otherwise collapse away and the replay would
    count the sample's label change twice.  The entry must also
    explicitly carry both ``old`` and ``new`` on every record first (see
    :func:`require_intact_history_labels`): a row missing either key is
    corruption too, never an unlabeled label to guess, and it is reported
    before the replay or the conflict verdict — an entry that would
    otherwise conflict is refused for the damage instead.  Explicitly
    saved ``null`` and ``""`` stay ordinary unlabeled labels and take
    part in the comparison as usual.
    """
    if existing is None:
        return None
    require_intact_history_records(existing)
    require_intact_history_labels(existing)
    if content_key(existing["records"]) == content_key(records):
        return replay_result(existing)
    raise BatchError(
        f"batch number {number!r} is already used with different content"
    )


def verify_records(
    records: list[dict[str, Any]], current_label: CurrentLabels
) -> list[BatchResolution]:
    """Verify every expected old label and classify each record, in one pass.

    Each record's current label is looked up once and used for both
    decisions: a current label differing from the expected old rejects the
    whole batch; otherwise the record is classified as changed only when
    the target label differs from that same current label.  No manifest
    item is modified here.
    """
    resolutions: list[BatchResolution] = []
    for record in records:
        current = current_label(record["sha256"])
        if current != record["old"]:
            raise BatchError(
                f"change for {record['sha256']}: expected old label "
                f"{render_label(record['old'])!r} but current label is "
                f"{render_label(current)!r}"
            )
        resolutions.append(
            BatchResolution(
                sha256=record["sha256"],
                old=record["old"],
                new=record["new"],
                current=current,
                changed=current != record["new"],
            )
        )
    return resolutions


def apply_resolutions(
    resolutions: list[BatchResolution],
    items: Mapping[str, dict[str, Any]],
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Mutate manifest items for the resolved records and build history rows.

    This is the only stage that changes samples: records flagged
    ``changed`` receive their target label and a new revision; no-op
    records keep both.  Every row additionally records the revision after
    the batch, which later undos pin against.  The pre-change revision is
    read from each item here, once, rather than during verification.
    """
    applied: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for resolution in resolutions:
        item = items[resolution.sha256]
        revision = item_revision(item)
        if resolution.changed:
            item["label"] = resolution.new
            revision += 1
            item["rev"] = revision
        applied.append(
            {
                "sha256": resolution.sha256,
                "old": resolution.old,
                "new": resolution.new,
                "changed": resolution.changed,
                "rev": revision,
            }
        )
    return applied


def build_history_entry(
    number: str, applied_records: list[dict[str, Any]]
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Assemble the history row for a batch with at least one change."""
    return {
        "batch": number,
        "records": applied_records,
        "changed_count": sum(1 for record in applied_records if record["changed"]),
        "undone": False,
        "undone_at": None,
    }


def result_payload(
    number: str, status: str, applied_records: list[dict[str, Any]]
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Build the user-facing result, keeping the original count meanings.

    ``changed`` counts records that actually changed a label,
    ``unchanged`` counts target-equals-current records and ``total``
    counts every submitted record.
    """
    changed = sum(1 for record in applied_records if record["changed"])
    return {
        "batch": number,
        "status": status,
        "changed": changed,
        "unchanged": len(applied_records) - changed,
        "total": len(applied_records),
    }


def no_changes_result(number: str, total: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Result for a batch whose records all match their current labels."""
    return {
        "batch": number,
        "status": "no-changes",
        "changed": 0,
        "unchanged": total,
        "total": total,
    }


def replay_result(entry: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Reconstruct the original result from a stored history entry."""
    return result_payload(entry["batch"], "already-applied", entry["records"])


def item_revision(item: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
    """Read a sample's label revision, treating malformed stored values as 0."""
    value = item.get("rev", 0)
    return value if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) else 0


def describe_history_revision_problem(value: Any, *, present: bool) -> str | None:
    """Describe why a history record's ``rev`` is not a usable revision.

    Every batch-history sample record must carry ``rev`` as a genuine
    non-negative integer: the revision pinned for later undos.  Booleans
    (``True == 1``), decimals (``1.0 == 1``), numeric strings (``"1"``),
    ``null`` and a missing field are all rejected rather than coerced, so
    they can never compare equal to a sample's current revision.  Returns
    ``None`` when the value is valid.
    """
    if not present:
        return "missing 'rev' field"
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return f"'rev' must be a non-negative integer, got boolean {value!r}"
    if not isinstance(value, int):
        return f"'rev' must be a non-negative integer, got {value!r}"
    if value < 0:
        return f"'rev' must be a non-negative integer, got negative {value}"
    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# History integrity checks
#
# Every ``require_intact_history_*`` check scans the same record list of
# the same target batch entry, so the shared mechanics live in two
# helpers: ``_iter_history_records`` reads the list once, rejects a
# missing list or a non-object row and yields ``(position, record)``
# pairs; ``_corruption_prefix`` and ``_record_ref`` assemble the common
# "Batch history is corrupted: batch ..." message parts.  The checks
# themselves stay separate passes and keep their original order on the
# undo path — duplicate digests, then revisions, then labels, then
# changed flags — each reporting its first problem in record order.
# Re-submission (``resolve_re_submission``) reuses the two checks that
# verdict needs, in the same order: duplicate digests, then labels, both
# running before the same-content replay / different-content conflict
# decision.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _corruption_prefix(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Shared prefix of every batch-history corruption message."""
    return f"Batch history is corrupted: batch {entry.get('batch')!r}"


def _record_ref(record: Mapping[str, Any], position: int | None = None) -> str:
    """Locate a history record by sample digest and optional 1-based position."""
    ref = f"sample {record.get('sha256')}"
    if position is not None:
        ref += f", record #{position}"
    return ref


def _iter_history_records(
    entry: Mapping[str, Any],
) -> Iterator[tuple[int, Mapping[str, Any]]]:
    """Yield ``(position, record)`` for each row of a batch history entry.

    This is the shared front half of every integrity check: the entry
    must carry a record list and every row must be an object.  Positions
    are 1-based, matching the record numbers used in error messages.
    """
    prefix = _corruption_prefix(entry)
    records = entry.get("records")
    if not isinstance(records, list):
        # validate_history() already rules this out; defend direct callers.
        raise BatchError(f"{prefix}: missing records")
    for position, record in enumerate(records, start=1):
        if not isinstance(record, dict):
            raise BatchError(f"{prefix}: malformed record")
        yield position, record


def require_intact_history_records(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Reject a batch entry whose records are not one row per sample.

    Undo pins every stored record to a sample content digest, so a digest
    may occur at most once in the target batch: a duplicated row — even a
    byte-for-byte copy, or a copy of a record that never changed a label —
    would otherwise restore the same sample more than once, bump its label
    revision repeatedly and inflate the restored count.  Duplicates are
    therefore batch-history corruption, never records to merge or
    de-duplicate.  The decision is independent of the labels, the
    before/after labels and the record's ``changed`` flag: the content
    digest alone decides.

    The whole record list is scanned, so rows preceding the repeat are
    checked too and a restorable row at the front can never mask a later
    duplicate.  On a repeat the error names the batch number, the sample's
    full digest and both 1-based record positions; nothing is repaired.

    Callers must run this before any success-shaped short-circuit (such as
    an already-undone batch or a same-number replay), so corruption can
    never be masked by a repeated-undo success or by a replay whose
    set-based content comparison would collapse the duplicate into one.
    """
    seen: dict[str, int] = {}
    for position, record in _iter_history_records(entry):
        digest = record.get("sha256")
        if digest in seen:
            raise BatchError(
                f"{_corruption_prefix(entry)}, sample {digest} "
                f"appears more than once, at record #{seen[digest]} and "
                f"record #{position}"
            )
        seen[digest] = position


def require_intact_history_revisions(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Reject a batch entry whose records lack a sound pinned ``rev``.

    Every record — changed or not — must carry ``rev`` as a genuine
    non-negative integer, since undo pins each changed sample to the
    revision it had at the end of the batch.  This is integrity damage,
    unlike the *manifest's* optional revision (see
    :func:`item_revision`, which keeps the legacy missing-means-zero
    behaviour): a bad row is reported with the batch number, the sample's
    full digest and the exact ``rev`` problem, and nothing is repaired.

    Callers must run this before any success-shaped short-circuit (such as
    an already-undone batch), so corruption can never be masked by a
    repeated-undo success.
    """
    for _position, record in _iter_history_records(entry):
        problem = describe_history_revision_problem(
            record.get("rev"), present="rev" in record
        )
        if problem is not None:
            raise BatchError(
                f"{_corruption_prefix(entry)}, "
                f"{_record_ref(record)}: {problem}"
            )


def describe_missing_history_labels(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str | None:
    """Describe which of a history record's before/after labels are absent.

    Every batch-history sample record must spell out both ``old`` (the
    label before the batch) and ``new`` (the label after it).  Only key
    presence is judged here: an explicitly saved ``null`` or empty string
    is a recorded unlabeled label, never a missing field.  Returns
    ``None`` when both keys are present.
    """
    missing = [key for key in ("old", "new") if key not in record]
    if not missing:
        return None
    if len(missing) == 2:
        return "missing 'old' and 'new' labels"
    return f"missing {missing[0]!r} label"


def require_intact_history_labels(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Reject a batch entry whose records lack a saved before/after label.

    Undo restores and counts samples purely from what the target batch's
    history rows say: a changed row is restored from ``new`` back to
    ``old``, an unchanged row is left alone.  That is only meaningful
    when every row explicitly carries both labels, so a row missing
    ``old``, ``new`` or both is batch-history corruption — never an
    unlabeled-to-unlabeled no-op to skip, and never something to guess
    from the sample's current label.  The error names the batch number,
    the sample's full SHA-256 digest, the record's 1-based position
    inside the target batch and which of ``old``/``new`` (or both) is
    absent; nothing is repaired, rewritten or restored.

    An explicitly saved ``null`` or empty string stays legal: both mean
    unlabeled, as does a literal class named ``unlabeled`` stay an
    ordinary label.  Only a missing key is damage.

    The whole record list is scanned in order — unchanged rows and rows
    behind restorable ones included — so a complete row at the front can
    never mask a damaged one further back, and no sample is restored
    before the damage is found.

    Callers must run this before any success-shaped short-circuit (such
    as an already-undone batch or a same-number replay), so corruption
    can never be masked by a success verdict or swallowed by a conflict.
    """
    for position, record in _iter_history_records(entry):
        problem = describe_missing_history_labels(record)
        if problem is not None:
            raise BatchError(
                f"{_corruption_prefix(entry)}, "
                f"{_record_ref(record, position)}: {problem}"
            )


def history_labels_equal(old: Any, new: Any) -> bool:
    """Whether two stored history labels describe the same category.

    The decision uses the labels saved in the history record itself, never
    a sample's current label: ``null`` and the empty string both mean
    unlabeled and are therefore equal, while every other value is compared
    as the exact original string — case, surrounding whitespace, Chinese
    text and path separators all keep their meaning, and a real class
    literally named ``unlabeled`` never equals unlabeled.
    """
    return normalize_label(old) == normalize_label(new)


def describe_history_change_problem(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str | None:
    """Describe why a history record's ``changed`` flag contradicts old/new.

    The flag must agree with the before/after labels saved on that same
    record: differing labels require ``changed: true`` and equal labels
    require ``changed: false``.  Returns ``None`` when the flag is
    consistent.  The stored labels are validated upstream as strings or
    ``None`` and the flag as a boolean, so no type guessing happens here.
    """
    actually_changed = not history_labels_equal(record["old"], record["new"])
    old_label = normalize_label(record["old"])
    new_label = normalize_label(record["new"])
    if actually_changed and not record["changed"]:
        return (
            f"'changed' is false but the before/after labels differ: "
            f"{render_label(old_label)!r} -> {render_label(new_label)!r}"
        )
    if not actually_changed and record["changed"]:
        return (
            f"'changed' is true but the before/after labels are identical: "
            f"{render_label(old_label)!r}"
        )
    return None


def require_intact_history_changes(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Reject a batch entry whose ``changed`` flags belie old/new labels.

    Undo restores a sample based on what the history row says the batch
    did: a row marked changed is restored from ``new`` back to ``old`` and
    counted, while a row marked unchanged is never restored.  So the flag
    must match the before/after labels saved on that row — judging from the
    record's own stored labels rather than any sample's current label:

    * differing old/new (``null`` and ``""`` being the same unlabeled
      spelling) require ``changed: true``;
    * identical old/new require ``changed: false``.

    A row that claims a change with identical labels would make undo count
    and restore a sample the batch never touched; a row that hides a real
    change would leave the sample at its post-batch label while the batch
    is recorded undone.  Both are batch-history corruption: the error names
    the batch number, the sample's full SHA-256 digest and the record's
    1-based position inside the target batch, together with the exact
    contradiction, and nothing is repaired.

    The whole record list is scanned in order, so a restorable row at the
    front can never mask a contradiction further back.

    Callers must run this before any success-shaped short-circuit (such as
    an already-undone batch), so corruption can never be masked by a
    repeated-undo success.
    """
    for position, record in _iter_history_records(entry):
        problem = describe_history_change_problem(record)
        if problem is not None:
            raise BatchError(
                f"{_corruption_prefix(entry)}, "
                f"{_record_ref(record, position)}: {problem}"
            )


def find_unique_history_entry(
    number: str, batches: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]
) -> Mapping[str, Any] | None:
    """Find the single history entry whose number is ``number``.

    An undo target must name exactly one batch.  Matching is on the batch
    number's saved raw string — no trimming of surrounding whitespace and
    no case folding — so the whole list is scanned with exact equality
    rather than stopping at the first hit: a second entry carrying the
    same number, whether adjacent to the first or separated by other
    batches, makes the target ambiguous.  Such a history is corrupted no
    matter what the two entries contain — identical record content,
    different samples, different label changes or differing undo states
    are all refusal, never a reason to pick the first, the last or the
    still-active one, and never something to merge.

    Returns the unique entry, or ``None`` when the number does not occur.
    On a repeat the error names the user-given batch number and the two
    1-based positions of the conflicting entries in the full history
    list, so neither record is undone, preferred or repaired.  Callers
    must run this before every per-entry integrity check and before the
    already-undone short-circuit: even an entry already marked undone
    leaves the number ambiguous and must surface this instead.
    """
    positions = [
        position
        for position, entry in enumerate(batches, start=1)
        if isinstance(entry, Mapping) and entry.get("batch") == number
    ]
    if not positions:
        return None
    if len(positions) >= 2:
        raise BatchError(
            "Batch history is corrupted: batch number "
            f"{number!r} appears more than once, at batch #{positions[0]} "
            f"and batch #{positions[1]}"
        )
    return batches[positions[0] - 1]


def empty_history() -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {"schema_version": BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION, "batches": []}


def validate_history(data: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Validate a loaded batch history payload; return it unchanged."""
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("schema_version") != BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION:
        raise BatchError("Unsupported batch history")
    batches = data.get("batches")
    if not isinstance(batches, list):
        raise BatchError("Malformed batch history")
    for entry in batches:
        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
            raise BatchError("Malformed batch history entry")
        if not isinstance(entry.get("batch"), str) or not entry["batch"].strip():
            raise BatchError("Malformed batch history entry: missing batch number")
        if not isinstance(entry.get("records"), list):
            raise BatchError("Malformed batch history entry: missing records")
        changed_count = entry.get("changed_count")
        if not isinstance(changed_count, int) or isinstance(changed_count, bool):
            raise BatchError("Malformed batch history entry: bad changed_count")
        if not isinstance(entry.get("undone"), bool):
            raise BatchError("Malformed batch history entry: bad undone flag")
        for record in entry["records"]:
            if not isinstance(record, dict):
                raise BatchError("Malformed batch history record")
            if not isinstance(record.get("sha256"), str):
                raise BatchError("Malformed batch history record: bad digest")
            for key in ("old", "new"):
                value = record.get(key)
                if value is not None and not isinstance(value, str):
                    raise BatchError("Malformed batch history record: bad label")
            if not isinstance(record.get("changed"), bool):
                raise BatchError("Malformed batch history record: bad changed flag")
    return data

211	        actual = set_totals[set_name]
212	        expected = Fraction(total) * ratios[j]
213	        if abs(Fraction(actual) - expected) >= 1:
214	            fail(set_name, "the overall count", actual, expected)
215	
216	    # Then each category on its own: a balanced total can still hide a
217	    # class whose samples were shifted between sets.
218	    for category in sorted(category_totals, key=_category_sort_key):
219	        category_total = category_totals[category]
220	        scope = "the unlabeled category" if category == "" else f"category {category!r}"
221	        for j, set_name in enumerate(SET_NAMES):
222	            actual = set_distributions[set_name].get(category, 0)
223	            expected = Fraction(category_total) * ratios[j]
224	            if abs(Fraction(actual) - expected) >= 1:
225	                fail(set_name, scope, actual, expected)

229	    return (0, "") if category == "" else (1, category)

233	    def __init__(self, root: Path) -> None:

245	    def initialize(self) -> None:
246	        # The empty-manifest decision is made under the workspace lock so a
247	        # concurrent first import cannot have its sample replaced by an empty
248	        # dataset created from a stale "manifest missing" observation.
249	        with self._locked(create=True):
250	            if not self.manifest_path.exists():
251	                self._write_json_atomic(
252	                    self.manifest_path, {"schema_version": 1, "items": []}
253	                )
254	            else:
255	                # An existing manifest is never rebuilt, emptied or
256	                # normalized away — but initializing over a structurally
257	                # broken one must not report success, so the corruption is
258	                # surfaced here exactly as for any other operation.
259	                self._read()

261	    def add(self, source: Path, label: str | None = None) -> ImportResult:
262	        # The label is validated before anything else — before the source
263	        # is even looked at — so an illegal label fails this call outright
264	        # and can never reach the manifest, not even on a re-import of
265	        # already registered content (which would otherwise report a
266	        # harmless "already present" success).
267	        _validate_import_label(label)
268	        self.initialize()
269	        file_path = source.resolve(strict=True)
270	        if not file_path.is_file():
271	            raise ValueError(f"Not a regular file: {source}")
272	        # Hashing is pure I/O on the source file; do it before taking the
273	        # workspace lock so concurrent imports of different files hash in
274	        # parallel and only serialize for the manifest check-and-commit.
275	        # The digest and the size must describe one stable file: the read
276	        # fails if the file's identity, size or modification time changes
277	        # around or during the read, so a source being rewritten or
278	        # replaced is rejected instead of registering a digest/size pair
279	        # that never coexisted.
280	        digest, size = self._read_stable(file_path, str(file_path))
281	        with self._locked(create=True):
282	            manifest = self._read()
283	            if any(item["sha256"] == digest for item in manifest["items"]):
284	                # Re-import never overwrites the registered source, label or
285	                # revision: the first report of a digest owns its metadata.
286	                return ImportResult(digest=digest, added=False)
287	            manifest["items"].append(
288	                {
289	                    "sha256": digest,
290	                    "source": str(file_path),
291	                    "size": size,
292	                    "label": label,
293	                }
294	            )
295	            manifest["items"].sort(key=lambda item: item["sha256"])
296	            # Commit through the same journal as batches so the import is
297	            # crash-safe and cannot clobber a batch committed concurrently.
298	            self._commit(manifest, self._read_history())
299	            return ImportResult(digest=digest, added=True)

301	    def import_directory(
302	        self, source: Path, label: str | None = None, recursive: bool = False
303	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
304	        """Import every accepted image file under a source directory at once.
305	
306	        Candidates are regular files (never symlinks or other entry types)
307	        whose lower-cased extension is one of :data:`IMAGE_EXTENSIONS`;
308	        recursion stays on the top level unless ``recursive`` is set and
309	        never descends through symlinked directories.  They are ordered by
310	        path relative to the source directory, with ``/`` separators,
311	        compared by Unicode code point.
312	
313	        Every candidate is read in full and identified by its full
314	        SHA-256 digest.  A digest already in the workspace, or first seen
315	        on an earlier candidate in this same import, is reported as a
316	        duplicate: the earliest sorted candidate owns the registration and
317	        later paths never overwrite its source or label.  The supplied
318	        label is attached only to genuinely new samples; ``None`` and the
319	        empty string both mean unlabeled.
320	
321	        The whole batch commits as one journal transaction.  The import
322	        fails entirely (no new samples) when the label is not a string or
323	        ``None``, when the source is missing or not a directory, a
324	        directory that should be visited cannot be scanned,
325	        a candidate cannot be read in full, a candidate's identity,
326	        size or modification time changes while it is being read, or a
327	        subdirectory confirmed as a real directory is replaced by a
328	        symbolic link before its scan or before its candidates finish
329	        reading — the link target's images are never imported or even
330	        reported as duplicates.  The label check comes first of all, so
331	        an illegal label fails the call even when the directory is empty
332	        or every candidate is already registered.
333	        """
334	        _validate_import_label(label)
335	        self.initialize()
336	        source_path = Path(source)
337	        if not source_path.exists():
338	            raise ValueError(f"source directory does not exist: {source}")
339	        if not source_path.is_dir():
340	            raise ValueError(f"source is not a directory: {source}")
341	        root = source_path.resolve()
342	
343	        rel_paths, confirmed_dirs = self._scan_image_files(root, recursive)
344	        # Read (and re-stat) every candidate before taking the workspace
345	        # lock: I/O overlaps with peers, and a file that changes mid-read
346	        # fails the whole batch before anything is committed.  A confirmed
347	        # subdirectory swapped for a symlink is never read through: every
348	        # candidate's ancestor directories are re-checked before it is
349	        # opened, the open itself is pinned to the confirmed ancestor
350	        # directories with O_NOFOLLOW descriptors, and the confirmed
351	        # directories are checked once more after all reads, so the link
352	        # target's images cannot be imported or even reported as
353	        # duplicates.
354	        candidates = []
355	        for rel_path in rel_paths:
356	            ancestor = root
357	            for part in Path(rel_path).parts[:-1]:
358	                ancestor = ancestor / part
359	                self._raise_if_now_symlink(ancestor)
360	            candidates.append(self._read_candidate(root / rel_path, rel_path))
361	        for directory in confirmed_dirs:
362	            self._raise_if_now_symlink(directory)
363	
364	        with self._locked(create=True):
365	            manifest = self._read()
366	            history = self._read_history()
367	            known = {item["sha256"] for item in manifest["items"]}
368	
369	            results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
370	            new_items: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
371	            for rel_path, abs_path, digest, size in candidates:
372	                if digest in known:
373	                    status = "duplicate"
374	                else:
375	                    status = "added"
376	                    known.add(digest)
377	                    new_items.append(
378	                        {
379	                            "sha256": digest,
380	                            "source": str(abs_path.resolve()),
381	                            "size": size,
382	                            "label": label,
383	                        }
384	                    )
385	                results.append(
386	                    {"path": rel_path, "sha256": digest, "status": status}
387	                )
388	
389	            if new_items:
390	                manifest["items"].extend(new_items)
391	                manifest["items"].sort(key=lambda item: item["sha256"])
392	                # One journal commit for the whole batch: an interruption
393	                # leaves either the old state or every new sample together.
394	                self._commit(manifest, history)
395	
396	        added = sum(1 for result in results if result["status"] == "added")
397	        duplicates = len(results) - added
398	        return {
399	            "directory": str(root),
400	            "recursive": recursive,
401	            "label": label,
402	            "candidate_count": len(results),
403	            "added": added,
404	            "duplicates": duplicates,
405	            "candidates": results,
406	        }

408	    def _scan_image_files(
409	        self, root: Path, recursive: bool
410	    ) -> tuple[list[str], list[Path]]:
411	        """Return accepted files and the real directories descended into.
412	
413	        The first element lists accepted files as ``/``-separated paths
414	        relative to root; the second lists every subdirectory confirmed as
415	        a real directory and descended into (empty unless ``recursive``).
416	
417	        Only real regular files qualify; symlinks and other entry types are
418	        skipped, and recursion never follows symlinked directories.  Any
419	        directory that should be visited but cannot be scanned fails the
420	        whole import with the path and reason.  Every confirmed
421	        subdirectory is opened through its pinned parent directory with
422	        ``O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW`` and scanned through that descriptor,
423	        so a subdirectory replaced by a symbolic link at any moment before
424	        or during its scan fails the whole import instead of the link
425	        target being scanned.  The confirmed list lets the caller
426	        re-verify the directories once more after the candidate reads.
427	        """
428	        rel_paths: list[str] = []
429	        confirmed_dirs: list[Path] = []
430	
431	        def classify(
432	            directory: Path, fd_or_path: Any
433	        ) -> list[tuple[str, bool, bool]]:
434	            try:
435	                entries = list(os.scandir(fd_or_path))
436	            except OSError as error:
437	                raise ValueError(
438	                    f"cannot scan directory {directory}: {error}"
439	                ) from error
440	            found: list[tuple[str, bool, bool]] = []
441	            for entry in entries:
442	                try:
443	                    is_file = entry.is_file(follow_symlinks=False)
444	                    is_dir = (
445	                        not is_file
446	                        and recursive
447	                        and entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False)
448	                    )
449	                except OSError as error:
450	                    raise ValueError(
451	                        f"cannot inspect entry {directory / entry.name}: {error}"
452	                    ) from error
453	                found.append((entry.name, is_file, is_dir))
454	            return found
455	
456	        def walk(
457	            directory: Path,
458	            rel_prefix: str,
459	            parent_fd: int,
460	            entries: list[tuple[str, bool, bool]],
461	        ) -> None:
462	            for name, is_file, is_dir in entries:
463	                if is_file:
464	                    if Path(name).suffix.lower() in IMAGE_EXTENSIONS:
465	                        rel_paths.append(rel_prefix + name)
466	                elif is_dir:
467	                    subdirectory = directory / name
468	                    # Open the confirmed subdirectory through the pinned
469	                    # parent with O_NOFOLLOW and scan the descriptor
470	                    # itself: a symlink swapped onto the path by now fails
471	                    # the whole import here, and the link target is never
472	                    # scanned.
473	                    try:
474	                        child_fd = self._open_real_directory(
475	                            name, parent_fd, subdirectory
476	                        )
477	                    except OSError as error:
478	                        raise ValueError(
479	                            f"cannot scan directory {subdirectory}: {error}"
480	                        ) from error
481	                    try:
482	                        child_entries = classify(subdirectory, child_fd)
483	                        confirmed_dirs.append(subdirectory)
484	                        walk(
485	                            subdirectory,
486	                            rel_prefix + name + "/",
487	                            child_fd,
488	                            child_entries,
489	                        )
490	                    finally:
491	                        os.close(child_fd)
492	
493	        try:
494	            root_fd = self._open_real_directory(str(root), None, root)
495	        except OSError as error:
496	            raise ValueError(f"cannot scan directory {root}: {error}") from error
497	        try:
498	            walk(root, "", root_fd, classify(root, root))
499	        finally:
500	            os.close(root_fd)
501	        # Unicode code point order on the slash-separated relative path.
502	        rel_paths.sort()
503	        return rel_paths, confirmed_dirs
504	
505	    @staticmethod
506	    def _open_real_directory(name: str, dir_fd: int | None, path: Path) -> int:
507	        """Open a confirmed directory, refusing a symlink swapped onto it.
508	
509	        The open uses ``O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW`` — relative to the
510	        pinned parent descriptor when ``dir_fd`` is given — so a symbolic
511	        link (or any non-directory) that replaced the confirmed directory
512	        is never descended through.  A symlink swap raises the import's
513	        "directory changed" error naming the replaced path; any other
514	        open failure propagates as the underlying :class:`OSError`.
515	        """
516	        try:
517	            return os.open(name, _DIRECTORY_OPEN_FLAGS, dir_fd=dir_fd)
518	        except OSError as error:
519	            # Linux reports a symlink opened with O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY
520	            # as ENOTDIR rather than ELOOP, so confirm via lstat() either
521	            # way.
522	            if error.errno in (errno.ELOOP, errno.ENOTDIR):
523	                try:
524	                    current = os.lstat(path)
525	                except OSError:
526	                    current = None
527	                if current is not None and stat.S_ISLNK(current.st_mode):
528	                    raise ValueError(
529	                        f"directory changed during import: {path} "
530	                        "is now a symbolic link"
531	                    ) from error
532	            raise
533	
534	    @staticmethod
535	    def _raise_if_now_symlink(directory: Path) -> None:
536	        """Fail if a previously confirmed real directory is now a symlink.
537	
538	        A path that vanished is left to the candidate reads (or ignored
539	        when the directory held no candidates); only the symlink swap is
540	        rejected here, because following the link would import the target's
541	        images against the no-symlinked-directories rule.
542	        """
543	        try:
544	            current = os.lstat(directory)
545	        except OSError:
546	            return
547	        if stat.S_ISLNK(current.st_mode):
548	            raise ValueError(
549	                f"directory changed during import: {directory} "
550	                "is now a symbolic link"
551	            )
552	
553	    def _read_candidate(
554	        self, path: Path, rel_path: str
555	    ) -> tuple[str, Path, str, int]:
556	        """Read one candidate in full, verifying identity/size/mtime around it.
557	
558	        Returns ``(rel_path, absolute_path, digest, size)``.  A mismatch or
559	        read failure raises before the batch is committed.
560	
561	        Every ancestor directory of the candidate is re-opened from the
562	        source root with ``O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW``, each relative to its
563	        pinned parent, and the candidate itself is opened relative to its
564	        pinned parent directory: a subdirectory replaced by a symbolic
565	        link since the scan fails the whole import here, and the link
566	        target's images are never opened — no matter when the swap lands.
567	        """
568	        parts = Path(rel_path).parts
569	        root = path
570	        for _ in parts:
571	            root = root.parent
572	        try:
573	            fd = self._open_real_directory(str(root), None, root)
574	        except OSError as error:
575	            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {rel_path}: {error}") from error
576	        try:
577	            ancestor = root
578	            for part in parts[:-1]:
579	                ancestor = ancestor / part
580	                try:
581	                    next_fd = self._open_real_directory(part, fd, ancestor)
582	                except OSError as error:
583	                    raise ValueError(
584	                        f"cannot read {rel_path}: {error}"
585	                    ) from error
586	                os.close(fd)
587	                fd = next_fd
588	            digest, size = self._read_stable(
589	                path, rel_path, dir_fd=fd, name=parts[-1]
590	            )
591	        finally:
592	            os.close(fd)
593	        return rel_path, path, digest, size
594	
595	    @staticmethod
596	    def _read_stable(
597	        path: Path,
598	        display: str,
599	        *,
600	        dir_fd: int | None = None,
601	        name: str | None = None,
602	    ) -> tuple[str, int]:
603	        """Read one file in full and return ``(digest, size)`` for it.
604	
605	        The digest and size are guaranteed to describe the same stable
606	        regular file: the path is lstat()ed without following symlinks
607	        and opened with ``O_NOFOLLOW``, the opened descriptor is
608	        fstat()ed to prove it is the inode that was confirmed, and the
609	        path is lstat()ed again after the read, requiring the same
610	        object with the same size and modification time.  Any identity,
611	        size or modification-time change — in-place rewrites, appends,
612	        truncation, delete-and-recreate, or replacing the path with
613	        another file, even one with identical content, size and mtime —
614	        fails with the path and reason, as do a vanishing path, a
615	        non-regular file and any open or read error.
616	
617	        The confirm/open/prove rule itself lives in :mod:`confirmed`
618	        and is shared with the source-directory export; only the
619	        post-read stability requirement and the import wording are
620	        specific to this entry point.
621	
622	        When ``dir_fd`` and ``name`` are given (whole-directory import),
623	        the pre-open inspection and the post-read re-inspection stay on
624	        the path, but the open itself is ``name`` relative to the pinned
625	        parent directory descriptor: an ancestor directory replaced by a
626	        symbolic link can never redirect the open into the link target.
627	        """
628	        try:
629	            if dir_fd is None:
630	                opened_file = confirmed.confirm_and_open_regular(path)
631	            else:
632	                confirmed_status = confirmed.inspect_regular(path)
633	                descriptor = confirmed.open_without_follow(name, dir_fd=dir_fd)
634	                opened_file = confirmed.ConfirmedOpen(
635	                    descriptor,
636	                    confirmed_status,
637	                    confirmed.prove_opened_regular(descriptor, confirmed_status),
638	                )
639	        except confirmed.ConfirmationError as failure:
640	            raise _import_confirmation_error(failure, display) from failure
641	        try:
642	            digest = confirmed.hash_descriptor(opened_file.descriptor)
643	        except OSError as error:
644	            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {display}: {error}") from error
645	        # Import, unlike export, also requires the path itself to still
646	        # name the same unchanged file after the read: an in-place
647	        # rewrite, append, truncation or replacement that landed while
648	        # the bytes were streamed must not register a digest/size pair
649	        # that never coexisted.
650	        try:
651	            after = os.lstat(path)
652	        except OSError as error:
653	            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {display}: {error}") from error
654	        if not confirmed.same_identity_size_mtime(opened_file.confirmed, after):
655	            raise ValueError(
656	                f"file changed during import: {display} "
657	                "(identity, size or modification time changed)"
658	            )
659	        return digest, opened_file.confirmed.st_size
660	
661	    def summary(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
662	        self.initialize()
663	        with self._locked():
664	            items = self._read()["items"]
665	        labels = Counter(item["label"] or "unlabeled" for item in items)
666	        return {
667	            "items": len(items),
668	            "bytes": sum(item["size"] for item in items),
669	            "labels": dict(sorted(labels.items())),
670	        }

672	    def find_by_label(self, label: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
673	        """List samples currently registered under one exact category label.
674	
675	        Matching is exact on the current manifest label: case, surrounding
676	        whitespace and path separators are all kept literally, so ``"cat"``
677	        never matches ``"Cat"`` or ``"cat "``.  The empty string queries
678	        unlabeled samples — records whose stored label is ``None`` or ``""``
679	        — and every matching record's label is reported uniformly as
680	        ``None``.  A genuine class literally named ``"unlabeled"`` is
681	        queried with that text and never mixed with unlabeled samples,
682	        unlike :meth:`summary` which merges them under one display key.
683	
684	        Each record provides the full SHA-256 digest, the source path saved
685	        at first registration, the byte size and the current label;
686	        records are sorted ascending by full digest and ``count`` always
687	        equals the list length.  The query reads the registered records
688	        only — it never opens a source file, and saved split plans' old
689	        labels are neither matched nor rewritten — so a moved, deleted or
690	        unreadable source is still found, and a batch update or undo
691	        committed before the call is immediately reflected.
692	        """
693	        if not isinstance(label, str):
694	            raise BatchError("query label must be a string")
695	        want_unlabeled = label == ""
696	        samples: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
697	        self.initialize()
698	        with self._locked():
699	            items = self._read()["items"]
700	        for item in items:
701	            stored = item.get("label")
702	            if want_unlabeled:
703	                if not (stored is None or stored == ""):
704	                    continue
705	                current = None
706	            else:
707	                if stored != label:
708	                    continue
709	                current = stored
710	            samples.append(
711	                {
712	                    "sha256": item["sha256"],
713	                    "source": item["source"],
714	                    "size": item["size"],
715	                    "label": current,
716	                }
717	            )
718	        samples.sort(key=lambda sample: sample["sha256"])
719	        return {"label": label, "count": len(samples), "samples": samples}

725	    def lookup_label(self, digest: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
726	        """Return ``{"sha256": digest, "label": str | None}`` for a sample.
727	
728	        ``None`` means unlabeled (the manifest may store ``null`` or ``""``).
729	        """
730	        with self._locked():
731	            manifest = self._read()
732	            for item in manifest["items"]:
733	                if item["sha256"] == digest:
734	                    return {"sha256": digest, "label": normalize_label(item.get("label"))}
735	        raise BatchError(f"sample not found: {digest}")

737	    def submit_batch_file(self, path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:

740	            data = json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

745	    def submit_batch(self, data: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
746	        """Validate and apply a batch label update.
747	
748	        Parsing happens before the lock; inside the lock the submission
749	        runs through clearly separated stages, each with one job:
750	
751	        1. **Unknown samples** — every named digest must be registered; the
752	           first unknown one rejects the batch with nothing written.
753	        2. **Number identity** — a batch number already in history is
754	           refused outright when that history batch is damaged: it may
755	           list each sample at most once (a repeated full SHA-256 digest,
756	           however the copies differ, is corruption), and every one of
757	           its records must explicitly save both the before (``old``)
758	           and after (``new``) label (an explicit ``null``/``""`` counts
759	           as saved).  The refusals come before either verdict below.
760	           An intact known number then replays the first submission's
761	           result (same content) or conflicts (different content);
762	           neither touches the manifest.
763	        3. **Verification/classification** — each current label is read
764	           once: an expected-old mismatch rejects the batch, and the same
765	           reading decides whether that record actually changes.
766	        4. **Application** — only records classified as changed are
767	           mutated; if none are, the batch occupies no number and writes
768	           no history.
769	        5. **History and save** — the entry and result are assembled from
770	           the applied records, and manifest plus history commit together
771	           through the journal.
772	
773	        No stage mutates anything before every earlier stage has passed, so
774	        a rejection can neither leave partially updated samples nor a
775	        partial history entry.
776	        """
777	        number, records = parse_batch_file(data)
778	        with self._locked(create=True):
779	            manifest = self._read()
780	            history = self._read_history()
781	            items = {item["sha256"]: item for item in manifest["items"]}
782	
783	            # Stage 1: every record must name a registered sample.
784	            reject_unknown_samples(records, items.__contains__)
785

790	            # saved old/new label) before it can compare or replay
791	            # anything.

793	                (entry for entry in history["batches"] if entry["batch"] == number),

801	            # unchanged in a single current-label pass.

805	            )

808	            # occupies no batch number and writes no history.

810	                return no_changes_result(number, len(records))
811	            applied_records = apply_resolutions(resolutions, items)

813	            # Stage 5: assemble history, then save manifest and history
814	            # together through the journal.

820	    def undo_batch(self, number: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
821	        """Undo a successful batch by number.
822	
823	        Only samples the batch actually changed are checked: each must have
824	        the same label revision it had right after the batch (no later
825	        modification, even one that restored the same label).  Repeated
826	        undos are idempotent and do not add history.
827	
828	        Integrity comes before either verdict.  First the requested number
829	        must identify exactly one entry in the saved batch list: a second
830	        entry carrying that same number — identical content or different,
831	        adjacent or separated by other batches, already undone or not — is
832	        batch history corruption, never a first-match/last-match/active
833	        choice and never a merge.  The target batch must then list every
834	        sample exactly once, carry a sound pinned revision on each
835	        record, explicitly save both before/after labels on each record,
836	        and have every record's ``changed`` flag agree with the
837	        before/after labels saved on that same record.  A duplicated
838	        number, a duplicated digest, a bad row, a missing label field or a
839	        flag that contradicts its labels rejects the undo even when the
840	        batch is already marked undone, so corruption is never hidden
841	        behind an ``already-undone`` success or confused with a sample
842	        modified after the batch.
843	        """
844	        with self._locked(create=True):
845	            manifest = self._read()
846	            history = self._read_history()
847	            entry = find_unique_history_entry(number, history["batches"])
848	            if entry is None:
849	                raise BatchError(f"unknown batch number: {number!r}")
850	
851	            # find_unique_history_entry scans the whole list, so a second
852	            # same-number entry — adjacent or behind other batches,
853	            # identical content or different, already undone or active —
854	            # raises before this point; repeats of other numbers do not
855	            # match and stay irrelevant.
856	            #
857	            # Validate the unique target batch's integrity — one row per
858	            # sample, sound pinned revisions, both before/after labels
859	            # saved, and a changed flag that matches those labels — before
860	            # the already-undone short-circuit and the later-modification
861	            # checks: a duplicated, inconsistent or corrupt history record
862	            # is refusal, not an undo, a no-op or an unknown batch, and
863	            # nothing is rewritten.
864	            require_intact_history_records(entry)
865	            require_intact_history_revisions(entry)
866	            require_intact_history_labels(entry)
867	            require_intact_history_changes(entry)
868	
869	            if entry["undone"]:
870	                return {"batch": number, "status": "already-undone", "restored": 0}
871	
872	            items = {item["sha256"]: item for item in manifest["items"]}
873	            for record in entry["records"]:
874	                if not record["changed"]:
875	                    continue
876	                item = items.get(record["sha256"])
877	                if item is None:
878	                    raise BatchError(
879	                        f"cannot undo batch {number!r}: sample {record['sha256']} "
880	                        "is no longer in the manifest"
881	                    )
882	                current = normalize_label(item.get("label"))
883	                # record["rev"] is now known to be a genuine non-negative
884	                # integer, so a boolean/decimal/string can never compare
885	                # equal to the sample's current revision.  The stored
886	                # after-label is normalized before comparing: history may
887	                # explicitly save either unlabeled spelling (null or ""),
888	                # and both match a sample currently unlabeled either way.
889	                if item_revision(item) != record["rev"] or current != normalize_label(
890	                    record["new"]
891	                ):
892	                    raise BatchError(
893	                        f"cannot undo batch {number!r}: sample {record['sha256']} "
894	                        "was modified after the batch"
895	                    )
896	
897	            restored = 0
898	            for record in entry["records"]:
899	                if not record["changed"]:
900	                    continue
901	                item = items[record["sha256"]]
902	                item["label"] = record["old"]
903	                item["rev"] = item_revision(item) + 1
904	                restored += 1
905	
906	            entry["undone"] = True
907	            entry["undone_at"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
908	            self._commit(manifest, history)
909	            return {"batch": number, "status": "undone", "restored": restored}

920	    @contextmanager
921	    def _workspace_lock(self):
922	        """Exclusive workspace lock for check-and-write transactions.
923	
924	        ``flock`` is advisory but sufficient for local processes: holders
925	        serialize, so every read-modify-write observes the state left by the
926	        previous completed operation.
927	        """
928	        self.state_directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
929	        descriptor = os.open(self.lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
930	        try:
931	            fcntl.flock(descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
932	            yield
933	        finally:
934	            try:
935	                fcntl.flock(descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
936	            finally:
937	                os.close(descriptor)
